The first ended in yaz on the revert pull's merge (405); the next two, each a new cycle, judged the same merge red again and ended 'ApiError: 422: POST git/refs; GitHub: Reference already exists (written: nothing)': the revert's branch brain/revert/<merge sha> stood from the first, with its open pull. Three things no page states, each with what the build does meanwhile. (1) What a cycle does with a revert an earlier cycle began and did not finish. asama-1/05:31-32 says yaz reverts the merge with gate.revert; 07 and 29i/29j describe one revert from nothing; no page names a branch or a pull that already stands. The build (this push, target.write 'Standing revert') takes the standing branch up only when its head is exactly the revert's commit (first parent's tree, the merge as its one parent), takes up the one open pull from it into brain/integration that GitHub lists for that head (GET commits/<sha>/pulls, a new read route of the writer's guard), opens one when there is none, and refuses anything else (revert_branch_differs) with nothing written. If the seed wants another rule (a new branch name per attempt, or deleting the old ref, which the guard forbids today), the page should say it. (2) Where such a cycle shows. 26f:17-18 fixes the revert row's payload as {merge_sha, head_sha}; neither that row nor the yaz job's line has a place that says the revert's branch or pull was taken up from an earlier cycle, or that a merge was sent more than once before GitHub accepted it (the resend of the last push). The build adds no field; the facts are in the writer's call list only and are lost with the job. A reader of the ledger cannot tell a revert finished in one cycle from one that took three. (3) Whether the yaz job's reason hard_stop for a failed GitHub write is 28's hard stop. 28:35-47 lists the triggers of a hard stop (a failed GitHub write to the target is not among them, a failed activation or transfer is) and says nothing is written until the operator lifts it. The loop's job ends reason hard_stop on any ApiError after its first write, persists nothing, and the next scheduled cycle runs and writes (observed: the two runs above started and reached yaz with no operator step). This push's take-up depends on that reading: under the other reading the standing revert would wait for the operator and the red merge would stay on brain/integration meanwhile. The page should say which, and if it is 28's stop, where the stop is kept so that the next cycle reads it.
